responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the TILEPro architecture, covering the machine model, ABI, instruction selection, scheduling, and target-specific front-end/runtime interfaces needed to generate code for TILEPro systems. Its core implementation files define target hooks for calling conventions, register and frame usage, address legality, costs, prologue/epilogue generation, PIC/TLS handling, builtin expansion, profiling, and assembler output, while the main machine-description files supply RTL patterns, predicates, constraints, and instruction attributes that map generic GCC RTL onto legal TILEPro instructions and bundle/scheduling behavior. Supporting files define TILEPro-specific modes, command-line options, C-family predefined macros, Linux OS/ELF overrides, and generated tables plus generator logic for efficient multiply-by-constant expansion, making the module the complete architecture-specific code generation and ABI layer that distinguishes TILEPro from neighboring GCC target ports.
